reading.body:
Julie Fedorchak's AI record shows more money from AI company PACs than AI legislation she has sponsored, with six contributions from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta committees against two AI bill cosponsorships.

The contributions run from June 2025 to August 2026 and total $14,500 in positive receipts, offset by one $2,000 refund from Google in July 2025. Microsoft's PAC gave twice, $5,000 each time. Google's committee appears four times. The two cosponsorships are the Small AI Innovators Empowerment Act in March 2026 and the TAKE IT DOWN Act in January 2025. Four recorded votes on AI bills all passed as Yeas.

For AI specifically, this is the money side of the compute buildout's political footprint. The companies funding data centers and power contracts are the same ones writing checks to members who sit on the committees that oversee them. The record does not show causation, and the page says so. It also does not show what Fedorchak did in committee, what she said about any bill, or whether any contribution preceded or followed any vote in a way that matters.

What the data cannot tell a reader is the size of these sums relative to her total fundraising, or how they compare to other members. Sixteen events over twenty months is a thin record. It establishes that AI industry PACs treat her as worth funding and that she votes yes on AI bills that reach the floor. It does not establish influence, and it does not measure her role in shaping the compute and grid policy that the industry's checks are ultimately about.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Julie Fedorchak: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 16 events.
